title: Cape Verde · Sal
blurb: Things worth knowing before (and while) you visit the island of Sal, Cape Verde.

questions.q: Cape Verde (Cabo Verde) lies off the coast of which part of Africa?
questions.fact: The islands sit in the Atlantic Ocean roughly 570 km west of Senegal.

questions.q: How many of Cape Verde's ten main islands are inhabited?
questions.fact: Santa Luzia is the only main island without permanent residents.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Cape Verde?
questions.fact: Praia is on the island of Santiago, not on Sal.

questions.q: What does the name 'Sal' mean in Portuguese?
questions.fact: Salt mining shaped the island's history long before tourism.

questions.q: What do the ten stars on the Cape Verde flag stand for?
questions.fact: They form a ring on the blue band, which stands for the sea and sky.

questions.q: In which year did Cape Verde become independent from Portugal?
questions.fact: Independence leader Amílcar Cabral did not live to see it; he was killed in 1973.

questions.q: Sal's international airport is named after which independence leader?
questions.fact: Amílcar Cabral International Airport is close to Espargos.

questions.q: What did the Portuguese find when they reached the islands in the 1400s?
questions.fact: People were brought to settle and work the islands, which is why Cape Verdean culture blends Portuguese and West African roots.

questions.q: What is the main tourist resort town on Sal?
questions.fact: Santa Maria sits at the southern tip, beside the long beach and the pier.

questions.q: Which town is Sal's administrative centre, close to the airport?
questions.fact: Most locals live in or near Espargos; the resorts are further south.

questions.q: What is the airport code for Sal's airport?
questions.fact: Look for SID on your boarding pass and luggage tags.

questions.q: Roughly how long is the island of Sal from north to south?
questions.fact: It is long and thin, so almost everywhere is a short drive from the sea.

questions.q: What is the highest point on Sal?
questions.fact: Monte Grande is only about 400 metres high. Sal is one of the flattest islands in Cape Verde.

questions.q: Which island group, named after a wind direction, does Sal belong to?
questions.fact: Barlavento means 'windward': the northern islands face the trade winds.

questions.q: Which neighbouring island is known for huge sand dunes and its main town, Sal Rei?
questions.fact: Boa Vista is a short flight or ferry ride from Sal.

questions.q: Where does most of Sal's drinking water come from?
questions.fact: Sal has no rivers and very little rain, so water is precious: don't waste it.

questions.q: Which landscape best describes most of Sal?
questions.fact: Sal is one of the driest places in Cape Verde, with sunshine nearly every day.

questions.q: When does Sal get what little rain it has?
questions.fact: Even then, showers are short and rare.

questions.q: What sometimes makes the sky hazy over Cape Verde?
questions.fact: The dusty haze is sometimes called 'bruma seca'.

questions.q: Which turtle species nests on Sal's beaches in summer?
questions.fact: Cape Verde is one of the world's most important loggerhead nesting sites. Never shine bright lights on nesting beaches at night.

questions.q: Which sharks do visitors usually see in the shallows at Shark Bay near Palmeira?
questions.fact: Follow your guide's rules and keep calm; most sharks there are young and shy.

questions.q: Which huge animals visit Cape Verde's waters in late winter and spring?
questions.fact: Trips from Sal and neighbouring Boa Vista sometimes get a glimpse of them.

questions.q: What do the steady north-east trade winds make Sal famous for?
questions.fact: Kite Beach near Ponta Preta is a favourite spot.

questions.q: What makes the crater at Pedra de Lume special?
a: A salt lake you can float in
A black-sand beach inside a volcano
questions.fact: Salt was mined from the crater; today you can bob in the very salty water.

questions.q: The 'Blue Eye' at Buracona looks its bluest when…
a: the tide is lowest at dawn
questions.fact: Daylight pours into the lava pool through a gap in the rock.

questions.q: What is the wooden pier in Santa Maria best known for today?
questions.fact: It's a lively spot early in the day and a popular place to watch the sunset.

questions.q: What is Cape Verde's national dish?
questions.fact: A slow-cooked stew of corn and beans with fish or meat. Leftovers are fried for breakfast.

questions.q: Which two things are the base of a traditional cachupa?
questions.fact: It cooks for hours, so locals often make it in big batches.

questions.q: Grogue, the local spirit, is made from what?
questions.fact: Mixed with honey or molasses it becomes 'ponche'. It is stronger than it tastes, so take it easy.

questions.q: Which Cape Verdean singer was known as the 'Barefoot Diva'?
questions.fact: She came from Mindelo on São Vicente and made morna famous worldwide.

questions.q: Which slow, soulful music style is Cape Verde best known for?
questions.fact: Morna songs are often about love, the sea and leaving home.

questions.q: What does the Cape Verdean word 'sodade' mean?
questions.fact: It is the same idea as the Portuguese 'saudade' and the title of Cesária Évora's best-known song.

questions.q: Which lively accordion-driven dance music is popular at Cape Verdean parties?
questions.fact: Funaná comes from the island of Santiago.

questions.q: Which island is considered Cape Verde's cultural capital, famous for its carnival?
questions.fact: Its main town, Mindelo, has a music scene that the whole country is proud of.

questions.q: Which Santiago town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.fact: It was the first European colonial town in the tropics.

questions.q: Cape Verdean Creole (Kriolu) is based mainly on which language?
questions.fact: Portuguese is the official language, but Kriolu is what people speak at home.

questions.q: Which of these is the local currency?
questions.fact: Euros are often accepted in tourist areas, but change usually comes back in escudos.

questions.q: The escudo is fixed in value to which currency?
questions.fact: It is about 110 escudos to the euro.

questions.q: Cape Verde is UTC−1 all year, with no clock changes. How far behind the UK is it in British summer time?
questions.fact: In UK winter it is just 1 hour behind.

questions.q: What plugs do you need in Cape Verde?
a: Two round pins (types C and F)
Two flat pins (the US type A)
Three flat pins (the UK type G)
Three round pins (the Indian type D)
questions.fact: It runs at 230 V like the UK, so you only need an adaptor.

questions.q: Which is the largest island in Cape Verde, home to the capital Praia?
questions.fact: Santiago is also where most Cape Verdeans live.

questions.q: Which small island is nicknamed the 'Island of Flowers'?
questions.fact: Brava is the smallest inhabited island and is reached by boat from Fogo.

questions.q: Which island is famous for wine and coffee grown on volcanic soil?
questions.fact: The vines and coffee bushes grow inside the huge crater of Pico do Fogo.

questions.q: Which island is known for steep green valleys and some of the best hiking in Cape Verde?
questions.fact: Its mountains catch the clouds, so it is far greener than flat, dry Sal.

questions.q: Which island do ferries from Mindelo travel to?
questions.fact: The crossing from São Vicente takes roughly an hour.

questions.q: What is the main town on the island of Fogo?
questions.fact: São Filipe has old colonial houses with wooden balconies.

questions.q: Which desert-like area on Boa Vista has sand blown in from the Sahara?
questions.fact: Boa Vista is the neighbouring island to Sal and has huge dunes.

questions.q: Why are Sal, Boa Vista and Maio so much flatter than the western islands?
a: The sea level rose and washed their peaks away
They were flattened long ago to make salt pans
They are made of coral rather than rock
They are older, so their volcanoes have worn down
questions.fact: The eastern islands are the oldest, which is why they have sandy beaches and little height.

questions.q: Which island was the first stop for Charles Darwin's voyage in 1832 after Tenerife?
questions.fact: HMS Beagle visited Santiago, which Darwin called St Jago, in January 1832.

questions.q: What does 'Cabo Verde' mean in English?
questions.fact: The name is a reminder of a headland on the mainland coast.

questions.q: Cape Verde is named after a headland on the African mainland. In which country is it?
questions.fact: Cap-Vert is on the coast of Dakar, about 570 km east of the islands.

questions.q: On which date is Independence Day celebrated in Cape Verde?
questions.fact: The islands became independent from Portugal on 5 July 1975.

questions.q: Who was the first president of independent Cape Verde?
questions.fact: He led the country from 1975 to 1991.

questions.q: Roughly how many people live in Cape Verde?
questions.fact: Many more Cape Verdeans live abroad than on the islands themselves.

questions.q: What is Cape Verde's international dialling code?
questions.fact: You'll dial +238 before a local number.

questions.q: Which side of the road do vehicles drive on in Cape Verde?
questions.fact: Remember this when crossing the road, especially if you're used to driving on the left.

questions.q: Cape Verde's people are proud of 'morabeza'. What does it mean?
questions.fact: It is the spirit of welcome that visitors often mention.

questions.q: What did Mindelo's Porto Grande harbour supply to passing steamships in the 1800s?
questions.fact: The port boomed because ships crossing the Atlantic needed to refuel.

questions.q: Which old fortress looks over the UNESCO town of Cidade Velha?
questions.fact: The hilltop fort was built to defend the town from pirates.

questions.q: Why did Sal's airport become important in the early days of long-distance flying?
a: It was a Portuguese military training base
It was the only runway long enough for early jets
It was the main sorting point for Atlantic mail
It was a refuelling stop in the middle of the Atlantic
questions.fact: The flat, dry island was ideal for a runway.

questions.q: Which community on Fogo was hit hardest by the volcanic eruption of 2014?
questions.fact: Lava destroyed villages inside the crater, and people have since rebuilt.

questions.q: About how tall is the volcano Pico do Fogo, the highest point in Cape Verde?
questions.fact: Its height is 2,829 metres, so it is a real mountain, not a hill.

questions.q: In which months do loggerhead turtles mainly nest on Sal's beaches?
questions.fact: Hatchlings head for the sea at night, so avoid bright lights near nesting beaches.

questions.q: What is 'pastel com diabo dentro' ('pastry with the devil inside')?
a: A fried pastry filled with sugar cane
A fried pastry filled with spicy fish
A sweet pastry filled with chilli jam
A baked pastry filled with goat cheese
questions.fact: The 'devil' is the hot pepper in the tuna filling.

questions.q: Xerém is a traditional dish based on what?
questions.fact: Corn is the heart of Cape Verdean cooking, from xerém to cachupa.

questions.q: What is the 'ferrinho' used in funaná music?
a: A small drum made from a gourd
A metal bar scraped for rhythm
questions.fact: Funaná is played with an accordion and a scraped iron bar.

questions.q: Which upbeat dance music is the livelier cousin of morna?
questions.fact: Coladeira has a quicker, more danceable beat than the slow, sad morna.

questions.q: In 2019, which Cape Verdean music was added to UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage?
questions.fact: Morna is often described as the soul of Cape Verde.

questions.q: Which Santiago tradition has women singing and drumming on rolled-up cloth?
questions.fact: The rhythm is beaten on cloth held between the knees.

questions.q: In Kriolu, what does 'Kuma ki bu sta?' mean?
questions.fact: Kriolu has different forms on different islands, but many people understand this one.

questions.q: On other islands, what is an 'aluguer'?
a: A stall selling fresh fish on the beach
A donkey you can hire for hill walks
A small ferry between nearby islands
questions.fact: Locals use aluguers to travel between towns; ask your hotel before using one.
